expectations.text: The check command exits 0 (no files created or changed)
The reply identifies path traversal via the file parameter (e.g. ../ or an absolute path makes os.path.join escape UPLOADS)
expectations.evidence: The reply says "`?file=../../../etc/passwd` climbs out of `/srv/app/uploads`" and "`?file=/etc/passwd` also works, because `os.path.join` throws away `UPLOADS` when the second part is an absolute path."

expectations.text: The reply names that any logged-in user can read files outside uploads, including other users' files, as the affected boundary
expectations.evidence: The reply says "anyone who knows or guesses a filename can download another user's upload" and "finding 1 stays reachable by any logged-in user," after saying the attacker can read "any file the app's process can read"; this covers both reading outside uploads and reading other users' files, though
